answer: Orchard Reach Diversity Rule: each identity’s reachable neighborhood must span distinct, previously unlinked clusters, measured as the smaller of two independent path sets. A juniper-labeled node joining many mutual clusters gets capped reach until those clusters show independent activity histories. An attacker must sustain separate, aged, non-interacting subgraphs per identity, so each fake identity costs ongoing maintenance of disjoint links plus delayed reach—not one cheap registration. The lagoon partition check rejects dense internal cycles shared across candidate identities.
